focus.jbig: Records hold into CPI week · scanner boarded 7 · Hormuz still live
focus.jtag: S&P 500 sits at a record after its best week since April; futures firm, but CPI Tue and PPI Wed are the week's real tests
focus.jnote: The backdrop is calm and record-setting — but a busy week is dead ahead. The S&P 500 closed Friday at a record ~7,758, capping its biggest weekly gain since April (S&P +3.58%, Nasdaq +5.19%) after July payrolls unexpectedly fell 23k and trimmed Fed-hike bets. Futures are modestly higher this morning as investors weigh softer jobs data and falling yields, with the VIX low near ~15.4. Two live overhangs keep it from being a clean green light: Iran said a Strait-of-Hormuz deal with Oman is in its final stages but will not reopen the waterway until the U.S. meets further conditions — keeping an oil-supply premium alive (WTI ~$78, Brent ~$83) — and the week's marquee macro prints, CPI on Tuesday and PPI on Wednesday, directly test the rate-cut narrative that lifted stocks.
focus.notdown: The scanner boarded six bullish names across Types A and C. CSWC is the cleanest — a Type C ATH breakout that HELD 3 sessions above its $24.30 pivot on ~1.65x volume with a 3-layer S/R stack and tradable options (OI 1,626, $0.10 spread) — the sturdiest name on the board and the only one that passed liquidity. AMGN, GHRS, SPXL (a 3x leveraged ETF), plus post-earnings gappers AAOI and UMAC also boarded bullish, but all carry near-zero relative volume, thin/unverified option chains, or both. Confirm each holds its level and the chain is actually tradable at 9:35 before selling any bull put.
focus.notup: One bearish name boarded — INTC (Type B). Note the tension: the scanner's catalyst text flagged semis/optics green pre-market, yet INTC is gapping DOWN this morning after announcing a proposed $15 billion stock offering that dilutes shareholders — a genuine bearish re-rate. But its options market was one-sided/unverified and IV is very high (~0.78), so any bear call carries violent-squeeze risk into a rising, record tape. Verify the chain and treat as watch-only unless liquidity and direction both confirm at 9:35.
focus.why: Why YELLOW, not GREEN? Composite is 38 (MILD) and P(≥1% gap) is ~31% (below the 35% trigger), which clears the numeric GREEN locks. But three things hold it at YELLOW: (1) CPI Tuesday and PPI Wednesday are inside a normal DTE window — scheduled index-gap risk; (2) the Strait-of-Hormuz reopening is an open-ended geopolitical tail keeping an oil premium alive; and (3) six of seven boarded names carry thin/unverified liquidity. Half size, A-grade only, keep DTE short enough to clear the inflation prints or wait for them to pass, and validate every chain at 9:35 ET.

risks: CPI · Tue 8/11 & PPI · Wed 8/12 — the week’s marquee macro prints and the direct test of the rate-cut narrative that lifted stocks to records. A hot number stacked on a fresh oil premium is the worst-case macro combo — keep any new spread’s DTE clear of them.

Strait-of-Hormuz reopening — Iran says a deal with Oman is in its final stages but will only reopen the waterway once the U.S. meets further conditions. Any breakdown sends crude (and the whole tape) gapping — the week’s biggest open-ended tail.
Oil & the 10-year — WTI ~$78 and Brent ~$83 keep an inflation premium alive; the 10Y is ~4.65%. A rate pop on top of an oil move pressures long-duration stocks right into CPI.
Heavy tech earnings week — Cisco (CSCO), Super Micro (SMCI) and CoreWeave (CRWV) all report this week; single-stock gaps can ripple through the AI/semis complex that led Friday’s rally.

Thin/unverified boarded liquidity — six of seven boarded names carry near-zero relative volume, thin OI, or an unverified/one-sided options chain (only CSWC passed). Verify each chain is real and tradable at 9:35 before selling anything — do not force a fill.

earnings.intro: Q2 season is in its tail stretch, but this week is busy on both macro and single-stock fronts — CPI (Tue 8/11) and PPI + retail sales (Wed 8/12) are the marquee catalysts, and Cisco (CSCO), Super Micro (SMCI) and CoreWeave (CRWV) report this week. Most boarded names carry NEXT-earnings dates ~52–62 days out (well outside a normal DTE), so single-stock earnings risk inside the trade window is low — but the CPI/PPI index-gap risk is not. Keep any new spread’s DTE short enough to clear the inflation prints.

rows.angle: Keep any new spread’s DTE clear of Tuesday, or wait for the print to pass. A benign number can reopen a cleaner, greener setup for later in the week.

rows.why: Cisco, Super Micro and CoreWeave all report this week — the AI/semis complex that led Friday’s record rally. A single-stock gap here can ripple through the whole tech tape and the boarded optics names (AAOI).

Disciplined stance: half size on A-grade only, verify each chain’s liquidity, keep DTE short enough to clear the inflation prints, validate at 9:35, and re-run the scan tomorrow pre-open.
